title: Ultrafast Electron Diffraction and Microscopy at Megahertz Rates
content: Ultrafast transmission electron microscopy [1] offers access to non-equilibrium dynamics on femtosecond timescales in spatially heterogeneous systems. However, the attainable contrast and resolution in diffraction and imaging is constrained by the comparably low electron brightness available from pulsed photoemission sources. In particular, the average electron bunch charge is limited by space-charge induced spatiotemporal pulse broadening affecting the available resolution. Higher repetition rates promise to circumvent these experimental constraints. However, as stroboscopic investigations rely on complete thermal relaxation in between subsequent excitation events, ultrafast microscopy is often at few-kilohertz rates or less. In turn, cycling ultrafast dynamics at higher duty cycles requires efficient thermal dissipation in thin material films.
